public_rationale: Marcus forecasts that the other three steps of his 2020 agenda (knowledge, reasoning, cognitive world models) will 'in time' be adopted. He gives no deadline. No decisive event shows leading systems built around all three in the sense of his paper, so the forecast stays open.
limitations: The terms are vague, and current industry uses of 'reasoning' and 'world models' may not match the paper's meaning.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The other three parts of Marcus's 2020 agenda (knowledge, reasoning, world models) will eventually be adopted, as neurosymbolic AI already has been.

statement.excerpt: The first part has already come to pass. In time, other three will, too.
statement.document_title: The biggest advance in AI since the LLM

from_speaker: The first part has already come to pass
In time, other three will, too
knowledge-, reasoning-, and world-model driven direction I laid out in 2020
our_interpretation: The 'other three' are the remaining steps of Marcus's 2020 paper: large-scale abstract knowledge, explicit reasoning, and cognitive (world) models.
'In time' sets no deadline, so the forecast is open-ended.
criteria.support_condition: Leading AI systems become publicly documented as built around large-scale explicit knowledge, explicit reasoning machinery, and explicit cognitive world models, as the 2020 paper describes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, no dated event can show the forecast false. The field abandoning these directions for good would weigh against it, but cannot settle it.
